headline: Software tools refine microbial taxonomy, SNP prioritization and host-read removal
label: Microbiome Sequence Analysis Tools
summary: Shotgun, amplicon and WGS datasets increasingly require reproducible, host-filtered and primer-aware processing before biological interpretation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is that upstream processing choices (host-read removal, classifier design, variant ranking, workflow structure) constrain the reliability of downstream microbial inference. A multi-step filter (Kraken2, BBDuk, multi-aligner) removes over 99.9% of human reads from rectal cancer WGS data, enabling Fusobacterium detection confirmed by immunohistochemistry. Parathaa addresses sequence ambiguity in amplicon data with primer-specific, region-level phylogenies, allows multiple labels per read, and outperforms IDTAXA. SNPraefentia ranks microbial metagenomic SNPs by depth, amino acid impact and UniProt domain annotation, while MeTAline packages shotgun taxonomic and functional profiling in containerized Snakemake workflows. The distinct contribution in this set is primer-aware handling of ambiguity in Parathaa; the MALDI-TOF MS Klebsiella study is a separate, non-sequencing diagnostic application.
